narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To explain a financial gap by contrasting the share of profits spent on stock buybacks among GM, Toyota, and Volkswagen.

units.meaning: Volkswagen's share of profits spent on buybacks is effectively zero in every year from 2012 to 2017 (table value 0.0035% each year), the lowest of the three companies.

basis.note: VW row; all VW years share this near-zero value
VW row; all VW years share this near-zero value
VW row; all VW years share this near-zero value
VW row; all VW years share this near-zero value
VW row; all VW years share this near-zero value
VW row; all VW years share this near-zero value

accepted_routes: VW does no meaningful buybacks in the period
VW is flat at the bottom, near zero, for all years
units.visual_evidence_rule: The VW series or mark must stay at or near zero across all years and visibly below GM and Toyota.
units.reviewer_question: Should VW's near-zero buyback share be obligatory, or is it only supporting context?

units.meaning: GM's buyback share is generally much larger than Toyota's and VW's; GM is above 80% in 2012 and 2014 and is the highest of the three in most years, but not in 2016.

basis.note: Exception year: GM is below Toyota

accepted_routes: GM is usually the highest buyback spender among the three
GM's buyback share is far above Toyota and VW in most years
GM is above 80% in 2012 and 2014 while Toyota and VW are much lower
units.visual_evidence_rule: GM's series must be visibly above Toyota's and VW's in most years, with the 2016 exception not contradicted.
units.temporal_anchor: how much of their profits these three companies spend on buybacks
units.reviewer_question: Should 'GM generally dominates Toyota and VW' be required, or is the specific 2016 exception enough?

units.meaning: Toyota's buyback share rises from near zero in 2013 to a peak of 39.0% in 2016, then falls to 19.0% in 2017; it remains much smaller than GM's peaks.
accepted_routes: Toyota climbs to its highest buyback share in 2016
Toyota's buyback share peaks at about 39% in 2016
Toyota's series rises from near zero in 2013 to a 2016 peak and then declines
units.visual_evidence_rule: Toyota's series must show a rise to its maximum at 2016 and a decline in 2017.
units.reviewer_question: Should Toyota's rise-and-peak trend be required, or is only the peak-vs-GM comparison needed?

units.meaning: In 2016, Toyota's buyback share (39.0%) is higher than GM's (28.0%); GM's 28.0% is its smallest value, so Toyota's biggest buyback year is roughly the size of GM's smallest.

basis.note: Toyota's largest value in the table
GM's smallest value in the table

accepted_routes: Toyota's largest buyback year is roughly comparable to GM's smallest
Toyota's 2016 peak (39%) is just above GM's 2016 low (28%)
Toyota's biggest buyback year is about 11 percentage points above GM's smallest
units.visual_evidence_rule: Toyota's 2016 point must be visible as higher than GM's 2016 point, and GM's 2016 point should be identifiable as its lowest.
units.temporal_anchor: Toyota's biggest buyback years are roughly the size of GM's smallest
units.reviewer_question: Should the 2016 Toyota-above-GM comparison be obligatory, or is the broader 'Toyota is much lower than GM' claim sufficient?

units.meaning: GM's 2017 buyback share is 112%, the highest value in the table and the only value above 100%.

basis.note: GM's maximum and only value above 100%

accepted_routes: GM spent 112% of profits on buybacks in 2017
GM's 2017 buyback share exceeds 100%, the only such point
units.visual_evidence_rule: GM's 2017 point must be visibly the highest and should read as exceeding 100%.
units.temporal_anchor: none in the provided narration; optional if the timeline includes 2017
units.reviewer_question: Should the 2017 >100% peak be required, or is it an optional striking detail?

optional_valid: Toyota's 2015 value (35.0%) is close to GM's 2015 value (36.0%), so 2015 is another near-parity year.
unsupported_to_avoid: Claiming VW did exactly zero buybacks; the table shows 0.0035%.
Claiming Toyota's biggest buyback is exactly equal to GM's smallest; it is 39.0% vs 28.0%.
Claiming GM always spends more than Toyota; GM is lower than Toyota in 2016.
Claiming buybacks caused the financial gap; the table only shows buyback share.
Extrapolating beyond 2012-2017 or using values not in the table.
notes: The core contrast is VW near zero, GM generally high, and Toyota's peak comparable to GM's low; the 2016 crossover and 2017 >100% are the most contestable inclusions. The 2017 >100% and Toyota trend are marked optional because the narration does not explicitly require them.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
